key_insight: Dopamine combines Cartesian-grid large-eddy simulation, free-surface tracking, and particle tracking to study small-scale turbulent physics in coastal waves.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports investigation of wave interactions with seabeds, coastal obstacles, and heavy or buoyant particles.
method: Geometric volume-of-fluid method on a staggered Cartesian grid tracks free-surface waves.
Ghost-cell immersed boundaries represent stationary solids; Vreman and AMD models represent sub-grid turbulence.
One-way-coupled Lagrangian tracking models heavy and buoyant point particles.
evidence_signal: Analytical, experimental, and numerical benchmarks assess waves and particle motion; two-fluid scaling efficiencies reach 77% strong and 73% weak at 512 CPU ranks relative to 64, with a single-GPU build verified against the CPU solver.
watch_item: One-way particle coupling neglects particle feedback on the flow, limiting applicability when particle loading significantly alters fluid motion.
paper_title: Dopamine: A Cartesian grid large-eddy-simulation framework for coastal ocean modelling of free-surface waves
